questions.def: First conditional: if + present simple, will + base form.
questions.question: If it rains, I ___ stay home.

questions.def: Second conditional: if + past simple, would + base form.
questions.question: If I won the lottery, I ___ travel the world.

questions.def: Zero conditional: if + present simple, present simple.
questions.question: If you ___ all your vegetables, you can have dessert.

questions.def: Third conditional: if + past perfect, would have + past participle.
questions.question: If I had studied, I ___ passed the exam.

questions.def: Second conditional question: What would you do…?
questions.question: What ___ you do if you lost your job?

questions.def: First conditional: if + present simple, not if + will.
questions.question: If she will study hard, she pass the exam.

questions.def: Third conditional: if + past perfect, would have + past participle.
questions.question: If I ___ to the party, I would have seen her.

questions.def: Zero conditional: if + present, present (general truth).
questions.question: If you heat water, it ___ boil.

questions.def: First conditional: will expresses future consequence.
questions.question: She ___ be angry if you don't call her.

questions.def: Second conditional: 'were' is often used instead of 'was' after 'if'.
questions.question: If I ___ you, I would apologize.

questions.def: Second conditional: if + past simple, would + base form.
questions.question: If I knew her number, I ___ call her.

questions.def: Third conditional: past perfect in 'if' clause, 'would have' in main clause.
questions.question: If he hadn't been late, we ___ missed the train.

questions.def: Second conditional: if + past simple, would + base form.
questions.question: If he ___ harder, he would pass the test.

questions.def: Second conditional: 'If I had' = past simple.
questions.question: If I ___ more time, I would learn to play the guitar.

questions.def: Second conditional: if + past simple.
questions.question: If she ___ the truth, she wouldn't be angry.

questions.def: First conditional: if + present simple, will + base form.
questions.question: She ___ you if she has time.

questions.def: First conditional: If + present simple, will + base form.
questions.question: If you exercise regularly, you ___ feel better.

questions.def: Third conditional: if + past perfect, would have + past participle.
questions.question: If they had listened, they ___ have understood.

questions.def: First conditional: if + present simple, will/won't + base form.
questions.question: If it ___, we won't go to the park.

questions.def: Second conditional: If + past simple, could + base form.
questions.question: If I were taller, I ___ play basketball.

questions.def: Third conditional: if + past perfect.
questions.question: If she ___ harder, she would have passed.

questions.def: Incorrect tense after 'if'. Use 'had studied' for the past perfect conditional.
questions.question: If I would have studied, I would pass the exam.

questions.def: First conditional: if + present simple, will + base form.
questions.question: If you ___ nice to me, I'll be nice to you.

questions.def: Zero Conditional: Scientific facts, if + present, present.
questions.question: If you mix yellow and blue, you ___ get green.

questions.def: Third conditional: If + past perfect, would have + past participle.
questions.question: If I had seen him, I ___ have said hello.

questions.def: First conditional: If + present simple, will + base form.
questions.question: If it rains, I ___ my umbrella.

questions.def: Second conditional: If + past simple, would + base form.
questions.question: If I won the lottery, I ___ a big house.

questions.def: Third conditional: use 'If I had' not 'If I would have'.
questions.question: If I would have known, I would have helped you.

questions.def: Second conditional: 'were' is used for all persons.
questions.question: If I ___ you, I would study harder.

questions.def: Unless = if not. First conditional: If + present, will + base.
questions.question: Unless you hurry, you ___ the bus.
